articles.summary: Strengthening our defenses against distillation attacks has made significant progress in recent months, reducing the effectiveness of distillation attacks on Claude by around 90 to 99 percent. These methods, which mimic frontier capabilities for a fraction of the development time and cost, have been used to extract capabilities from models without proportionally robust safeguards. As a result, distilled models could be used to cause significant harm in areas like biology and cybersecurity. Strengthening our defenses against distillation attacks is crucial to preventing the misuse of models and protecting national security, as illicitly distilled models can be integrated into foreign military, intelligence, and surveillance systems.

articles.title: Who is vfmaddrnd231pd?
articles.summary: vfmaddrnd231pd is a unique instruction from the FMA instruction set, defined in the Intel Software Development Manual as VFMADDRND231PD - Fused Multiply-Add of Packed Double-Precision Floating-Point Values with rounding control. This instruction allows for controlled rounding of floating-point values, potentially making some algorithms faster. However, it appears that the instruction is not recognized by GNU assembler, the Intel C/C++ Compiler, or other tools, and its implementation is not available in recent versions of the Software Development Manual.
